groups.name: Grammar
groups.description: Use English structures accurately in conversation.

items.title: Present simple – affirmative
items.can: I can talk about my routines and habits.
items.example: I play football. / She plays football.
items.lesson: Use the base verb with I, you, we and they. With he, she and it, usually add -s or -es.
items.assessment: Say three things you do every day, then describe a friend’s routine.

items.title: Present simple – negatives
items.can: I can say what people do not do.
items.example: I don’t like fish. / He doesn’t play tennis.
items.lesson: Use don’t or doesn’t before the base verb.
items.assessment: Say three negative sentences about your habits.

items.title: Present simple – questions
items.can: I can ask and answer questions about routines.
items.example: Do you play football? / Does she read books?
items.lesson: Do or does comes before the subject. Use the base verb after the subject.
items.assessment: Ask your teacher three questions and answer three questions without reading.

items.title: Present continuous
items.can: I can describe actions happening now.
items.example: She is reading. / They are running.
items.lesson: Use am, is or are + verb-ing.
items.assessment: Describe four actions in a picture.

items.title: There is / There are
items.can: I can describe what is in a place.
items.example: There is a chair. / There are two windows.
items.lesson: Use there is for singular and there are for plural nouns.
items.assessment: Describe your classroom using both forms.

items.title: Past simple – regular verbs
items.can: I can talk about completed past actions.
items.example: Yesterday I played football.
items.lesson: Most regular verbs add -ed in the affirmative past simple.
items.assessment: Say what you did yesterday using three regular verbs.

items.title: Comparatives
items.can: I can compare people, animals and objects.
items.example: A giraffe is taller than a zebra.
items.assessment: Compare three pairs of animals.

groups.name: Vocabulary
groups.description: Recognise, recall and use words in context.

items.title: Animals
items.can: I can name common animals and describe them.
items.example: a lion · a monkey · a crocodile
items.assessment: Name the animals from pictures and describe two of them.

items.title: Food and drink
items.can: I can name common food and drinks.
items.example: I like apples. / I’d like some water.
items.assessment: Name six foods from pictures and use two in sentences.

items.title: The house
items.can: I can name rooms and everyday furniture.
items.example: The sofa is in the living room.
items.assessment: Name objects and explain where they are.

items.title: Daily routines
items.can: I can talk about everyday activities.
items.example: I get up at seven.
items.lesson: get up · have breakfast · go to school · do homework · go to bed
items.assessment: Describe your day in order.

items.title: Clothes
items.can: I can describe what people are wearing.
items.example: He is wearing a blue shirt.
items.assessment: Name clothes and describe what someone is wearing.

items.title: Sports and hobbies
items.can: I can talk about activities I enjoy.
items.example: I like swimming.
items.lesson: football · basketball · tennis · swimming · drawing · reading
items.assessment: Name activities and say which you like.

groups.name: Reading & writing
groups.description: Understand short texts and write independently.

items.title: Spell familiar words from pictures
items.can: I can write familiar words with the correct spelling.
items.example: cat · school · pencil
items.lesson: Look at a picture, recall the English word and write it without a model.
items.assessment: Write six familiar picture words without copying.

items.title: One-word answers
items.can: I can answer simple questions about a picture.
items.example: How many dogs? — Two.
items.lesson: Read the question, identify the answer in the picture and write one word.
items.assessment: Answer five short picture questions in writing.

items.title: Complete sentences about pictures
items.can: I can write simple sentences to describe a picture.
items.example: The boy is riding a bike.
items.lesson: Use a subject, verb and the necessary details. Check capitals and full stops.
items.assessment: Write three independent sentences about a picture.

items.title: Read a short story
items.can: I can understand the main events in a simple story.
items.example: Who is in the story? What happens?
items.lesson: Read for the main idea, then look back for details.
items.assessment: Read a short text and answer comprehension questions.

groups.name: Speaking & listening
groups.description: Understand and communicate in everyday situations.

items.title: Personal information
items.can: I can answer questions about myself.
items.example: My name is… / I’m nine.
items.lesson: Practise your name, age, family and interests.
items.assessment: Answer simple personal questions without a script.

items.title: Classroom instructions
items.can: I can understand everyday classroom instructions.
items.example: Open your book. / Put the pencil on the table.
items.lesson: Listen for the action word and the object or place.
items.assessment: Follow five spoken instructions without translation.

items.title: Describe a picture
items.can: I can describe people, objects and actions.
items.example: There are two children. They are playing.
items.lesson: Look at who, what, where and what is happening.
items.assessment: Describe a new picture using several sentences.

items.title: Find differences
items.can: I can explain differences between two pictures.
items.example: Here the bag is red, but there it is blue.
items.lesson: Compare objects, colours, numbers and actions.
items.assessment: Describe three differences between two new pictures.
